sections.html:
With a median value of $156,200 and a large rental share, a house that needs work often sells to an investor. Those buyers pay cash, close on your schedule and buy as is, while a listed sale usually means repairs, showings and a lender's appraisal.

  • Decide whether the house is owner occupied, vacant or rented, since that sets the registration steps below.
  • Collect the deed, tax bills and any code notices.
  • Compare a cash offer to a listing by what you net after repairs and carrying costs.

Peoria is the largest city on the Illinois River in this part of the state, about 110,920 people now, down 2.0 percent from 113,150 in 2020. Only 57.5 percent of homes are lived in by their owners, so landlords and investors are a real part of the buyer pool.

Neighborhoods differ a great deal. Several areas, such as Averyville and El Vista, began as separate towns that the city absorbed, so a sale on the East Bluff, in the Uplands or in North Valley can look very different from one across town.

sections.h2: Registering a rental or vacant property
sections.html:
The city requires registration of rental properties, vacant residential properties and any dwelling the owner does not live in. Owners renew by February 28 each year. A new registration is due within 30 days after closing or after the home becomes non-owner occupied.

Fees listed by the city:

  • Renewal for a single-family home is $75. A multi-family property pays $75 for the first unit and $20 for each additional unit.
  • New single-family registrations cost $75 from January 1 to September 30 and $50 from October 1 to December 31.
  • A late registration fee of $150 per property applies after February 28 or more than 30 days after purchase.

You can register as exempt when the property is vacant and for sale, with an MLS or other listing as proof. The same goes for a property in probate or estate settlement, one where an immediate family member lives, one that holds a city Mothball Permit, or an owner-occupied home that is temporarily vacant for up to six months.

Owners who live outside Peoria, Tazewell and Woodford counties must appoint a local property manager. After a sale, tell the city and use the Change of Status form to deactivate the sold property's registration.

sections.h2: The Peoria transfer declaration at closing
sections.html:
The city's real estate transfer declaration carries a tax of $2.50 per $1,000 of consideration or part thereof. It also asks you to check whether the property will be owner occupied or non-owner occupied. If the non-owner box is checked, section 5-522(a) of the city code requires the property to be registered as non-owner occupied at the time of closing.

The form lists exemptions, including deeds where the actual consideration is less than $100, tax deeds, deeds that only confirm or correct a prior recorded deed, and deeds to or from governmental bodies.

The county side runs separately. Peoria County takes part in the state MyDec system, which allows the PTAX-203 to be submitted electronically before the deed is recorded. Ask your closing attorney or title company to prepare the city form alongside the county filing so nothing holds up the recording.

sections.h2: Which school district is your Peoria address in?
sections.html:
Peoria Public Schools District 150 serves most of the city. Dunlap Community Unit School District 323 serves the far north and northwest, and Pleasant Valley School District 62, Limestone Community High School District 310, Peoria Heights District 325 and Illinois Valley Central District 321 cover edge areas.

A few blocks can change a child's district, so give buyers the district name that matches the address and confirm it with the district first.

sections.h2: How does Peoria's weather affect older houses?
sections.html:
Peoria has a humid continental climate, with hot summers and cold winters. Swings that wide are hard on older roofs, flashing, chimneys and basement walls. A buyer's inspector will ask how old the roof, chimney and basement walls are and when they were last repaired. Collect receipts and permit records before you list, and be ready to say plainly what has been done.

If the house needs more work than you want to take on, that is the situation where an as-is cash sale makes the most sense, since the buyer prices the repairs into the offer and you skip the inspection back and forth.

sections.h2: What to gather before you close
sections.html: A Peoria sale goes faster when the paperwork is ready. Bring the deed, recent tax bills, any city code notices, and proof of listing if you plan to register a vacant property as exempt. Ask your closing attorney to confirm whether the non-owner box on the city declaration applies to the buyer. If the buyer is an investor who will rent the house, the new owner must register it as non-owner occupied at closing.

faqs.q: How much is the City of Peoria real estate transfer tax?
faqs.a: The city's transfer declaration carries $2.50 per $1,000 of consideration or part thereof. The form includes a list of exempt deed types. Ask your closing attorney to complete it with the PTAX-203 filed through the county.

faqs.q: Do I have to register a Peoria house I am selling?
faqs.a: Only if it is not owner occupied. Vacant homes listed for sale qualify for an exempt registration when you give the city an MLS or other listing as proof. After a sale, tell the city and use the Change of Status form to deactivate the registration.

faqs.q: When is Peoria's non-owner-occupied registration due?
faqs.a: Renewals are due every year by February 28, and new properties must be registered within 30 days after closing or after becoming non-owner occupied. A $150 late fee applies after those dates.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Peoria house in?
faqs.a: Most of Peoria is in District 150, but Dunlap District 323, Pleasant Valley District 62, Limestone District 310, Peoria Heights District 325 and Illinois Valley Central District 321 cover other parts. Check the address with the district before you list.

faqs.q: Is Peoria a good market for a quick cash sale?
faqs.a: A cash sale is an option for many houses. Investors and landlords are part of the buyer pool, so compare any offer against a listed sale after repairs, fees and carrying costs.
